Settings → Server / Hosts edits domain, ports, DNS, WireGuard public key, REALITY SNI list, obfuscation and CDN options live (no restart). Settings → Tunnel sets the public URL and trusted proxies — the latter decides whose X-Forwarded-For is believed for rate limiting and audit logs.

During install (step 7): Nginx reverse proxy + Let's Encrypt with auto-renew cron. From the panel (Settings → SSL): issue or renew a certificate for domain or sub.domain — standalone HTTP-01 on port 80, expiry shown in the panel. LAN / tunnel mode ( start-lan.bat ) serves the panel over plain HTTP. Anyone on that network can sniff your session — only use it on networks you trust, or reach the panel through an encrypted SSH tunnel instead.

s: “Too many attempts, try again in a few minutes”
t: You (or someone) failed login 8+ times in 15 minutes. Wait, then log in carefully. If it persists with the right password, restart the panel service — in-memory counters reset: systemctl restart zefira .

SSH into the server and set a new one via environment + restart, or edit ZEFIRA_ADMIN_PASSWORD in /opt/zefira/.env — note this only applies to a fresh database. On an existing DB, stop the service, delete instance/zefira.db (you lose data — restore from backup after), and restart to trigger first-ru
You forgot the X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest header — the CSRF guard. Browsers using the panel send it automatically.

systemctl status zefira journalctl -u zefira -n 100 --no-pager curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8000/login && echo PANEL-UP ss -tlnp | grep 8000 If the port is taken, another copy is already running — stop it before starting a new one.
Tokens rotate on Reset token — resend the new link. Check the user is active, not expired and not out of volume. If you renamed SUBSCRIPTION_PATH , old /sub/… links stop working.
Port 80 must be free and the domain's DNS must point at the server. Let's Encrypt rate-limits repeated issuance — wait an hour and retry. Behind Nginx, make sure the HTTP vhost exists before issuing.

s: Clients can't connect but the sub link loads
t: Open the VPN ports on the firewall ( ufw allow 443/tcp , plus inbound / Hy2 / WG ports). Verify Settings → Server domain/ports match reality, and the REALITY public key is generated. WireGuard shows a warning comment until you paste the server's public key in Settings.

s: Do I have to pay for any of this?
t: No. Zefira is MIT-licensed, the docs site is plain static files in this repo, and GitHub Pages hosting is free. Let's Encrypt certificates are free too. Zefira · MIT License · github.com/mrlurix/zefira

During install (or via SUBSCRIPTION_PATH ) you can rename /sub to anything, e.g. /s — links become https://domain/s/TOKEN . Obscurity is not security, but it cuts scanner noise. Zefira · MIT License · github.com/mrlurix/zefira

Open Users → New user . Pick a username (English letters, digits, _ , 3–32 chars). Select one or more protocols — any mix of VLESS, REALITY, VMess, Trojan, Shadowsocks, Hysteria2, WireGuard, OpenVPN. Set volume (GB) and duration (days). Optional: note, device limit, start-on-first-use. Save. The pan

Save recurring plans ( Templates ) — name, protocols, volume, days, first-use and device limit — then create users from a template in one click. Template names allow letters, digits, spaces, _ and - .

Extra ports per protocol ( Inbounds ): give VLESS port 443 and 8443, each with its own host. Subscription links and Clash configs include every enabled inbound automatically, labeled with the inbound name.

Register Iran ⇄ Kharej tunnels: transport, both IPs, tunnel port, forwarded ports, UDP flag. Zefira stores an encrypted token per tunnel, generates a step-by-step setup guide for both servers, and can probe the Iran endpoint ( Check now ) with automatic online/offline status.
